1.why: UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across cards and forms.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, and text is broken into short blocks rather than dense paragraphs.

3.why: Layouts are single-column cards with readable inputs and buttons that fit a mobile viewport without horizontal overflow.

4.why: Most instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as “Use an authenticator app to generate a code.”

5.why: No illustrative examples of expected input format are shown beside fields like verification or authenticator codes.

6.why: User can proceed via short labels and single buttons without reading long passages of text.

7.why: Secrets and recovery codes appear as selectable text that can be copied, but dedicated copy controls are absent.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent scannable alternative is offered; only manual secret and otpauth text are provided.

9.why: Email and phone fields look autofill-friendly, yet OTP/code inputs show no explicit password-manager or one-time-code attributes.

10.why: Page titles and primary blue CTAs clearly indicate the current step and main action.

11.why: Each screen focuses on one primary task with a single main button.

12.why: Feedback banners such as “Authenticator created” and “Recovery code confirmed” state outcomes and next actions.

13.why: Users can regenerate recovery codes, revisit MFA settings, and retry entry without lockout or penalty.

14.why: The observed error “Unable to complete this request. Please try again.” does not explain the cause or a concrete fix.

15.why: No countdown timers or expiry warnings appear on reading or code-entry screens.
